columns.label: Amp
columns.description: Amplitude (relative weight) of this lifetime component.

buttons.label: 📂 Load
buttons.description: Load a lifetime spectrum from a CSV/text file (interleaved a,τ list or 2-column amplitude/lifetime table).

sections.label: Bins
sections.description: Number of micro-time (TAC) bins in the decay histogram.

sections.label: Start
sections.description: Bin index where the ideal decay begins (prompt offset).

sections.label: IRF
sections.description: Optional instrument response function file (text or .npy) to convolve with the decay. Empty = ideal decay.

sections.label: Noise
sections.description: Poisson-sample a finite-count observation (uses Photons + Seed). Off = normalized ideal pattern.

sections.label: Photons
sections.description: Total photon count for the Poisson observation.

sections.label: Seed
sections.description: Random seed for the shot-noise realization (reproducible).

sections.label: Mode
sections.description: Detection mode. VM: magic angle — the decay carries no anisotropy. VV/VH: parallel and perpendicular channels generated with the rotation spectrum below; both share one photon budget when Noise is on.

sections.label: g
sections.description: Parallel/perpendicular detection sensitivity ratio G. The perpendicular channel records 1/G of what an equally sensitive one would.

sections.label: l1
sections.description: Polarization mixing factor of the parallel (VV) channel.

sections.label: l2
sections.description: Polarization mixing factor of the perpendicular (VH) channel.

columns.label: b
columns.description: Amplitude of this rotational correlation component. The b amplitudes sum to the fundamental anisotropy r0.

columns.label: ρ
columns.description: Rotational correlation time in nanoseconds. r(t) = Σ bᵢ exp(−t/ρᵢ).

buttons.label: ➖ Remove
buttons.description: Remove the selected rotational correlation component.

buttons.label: 🧪 Generate
buttons.description: Generate the decay and update the plot.

buttons.label: 💾 Save
buttons.description: Save the generated decay (CSV / text / .npy / JSON). In VV/VH mode writes a VV/VH file whose footer carries g, l1, l2 and the mode.

buttons.label: 🔗 Fit group
buttons.description: Add the generated data as a dataset and create a fit group with the Lifetime model — same route as a VV/VH data load: VV and VH become group members with vv/vh polarizations and g, l1, l2 are carried over from the simulation.

sections.title: Synthetic decay
sections.description: The generated fluorescence-decay histogram. VV/VH mode shows both polarized channels.

sections.title: Anisotropy r(t)
sections.description: The anisotropy decay r(t) = Σ bᵢ exp(−t/ρᵢ) of the rotation spectrum, shown in both modes (the VM decay itself carries no anisotropy).
